correctness.rationale: For every m>=3, the sufficiently subdivided two-particle Abrams complex gives exact chain modules. An integral two-cycle must have coefficients constant along each branch in both coordinates; each such coefficient is zero because the two first edges share the same pole and hence are prohibited in a two-cell. This injects the degree-two boundary integrally. The ordered complex is connected, so the degree-one character equals 1 minus the signed alternating chain trace. Explicit cell counts for all four combinations of pole reversal and label exchange give tr H1(σρ^hτ^b)=(-1)^h[f(f-1)-1 if b=0, 1-2t if b=1]. This is exactly the character of the signed ordered-pair representation modulo its total-sum line. Rational semisimplicity yields the module. Transfer identifies the unordered action with the exterior-square positive eigenspace. The embedded verifier independently checks 672 cases and modular boundary ranks through six branches; those finite checks corroborate but do not replace the universal argument.

value.rationale: For two moving particles on a canonical family of multiply connected networks, the branch-permutation, pole-reversal and particle-exchange actions are physically and topologically natural. Their first-homology representation determines all action traces and invariant subspaces and distinguishes ordered from unordered particles; these data cannot be read from Betti ranks or abstract free-group presentations. The complete uniform m>=3 classification and anti/symmetric pair decomposition are structural and mathematically motivated. No downstream theorem or broad publication claim is necessary for the value of this precise representation classification.
